definition: A progressive disease characterized by lung scarring, stiffness, and impaired healing from damage or inflammation.
general_symptoms: Shortness of breath, especially during or soon after exertion
Dry cough that doesn’t go away
Bluish, gray or white skin around your lips, eyes or nails (cyanosis)
general_causes: Lungs not healing properly from damage or inflammation
Connective tissue disease (rheumatoid arthritis (RA), lupus, scleroderma)
Environmental exposures (asbestos, silica, beryllium, hypersensitivity pneumonitis from certain molds, bacteria, or bits of bird feathers/droppings)
Medications or treatments (amiodarone, nitrofurantoin, methotrexate, radiation therapy)
general_diagnosis_methods: Ruling out other conditions that affect heart and lungs
Blood tests, including an arterial blood gas
general_treatments: Medications to treat underlying causes (like autoimmune disease) or conditions that make scarring worse (like GERD)
general_outlook: Permanent and usually gets progressively worse over time
Lung scarring is nearly always permanent (unless caused by a medication and caught early)
Healthcare providers can't easily predict how it will progress; symptoms may get worse very slowly over years or lead to severe symptoms quickly over months
complications: Low oxygen in your blood (hypoxemia) and tissues (hypoxia)
High blood pressure in your lungs (pulmonary hypertension)
prevention: Avoiding substances that can harm your lungs (asbestos, metal dust, chemicals) and wearing a respirator mask if working with them
Avoiding things that can cause chronic allergic reactions (hay, grain, bird droppings, feathers, heating/cooling systems) and wearing a respirator mask if working with them
living_with: Washing hands frequently, disinfecting surfaces, and avoiding crowded places
Getting recommended vaccinations (pneumonia, flu, RSV, COVID)

etiology_and_subtypes.definition: Form of pulmonary fibrosis with an unknown cause.
life_expectancy: Three to five years for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (though life expectancies have been getting longer in recent years)

causes: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis (from certain molds, bacteria, or bits of bird feathers/droppings)
